hotspots.trendWarning: Haze trajectory deteriorating over past 3 hours
hotspots.trendImproving: Haze trajectory improving over past 3 hours
hotspots.practicalTipElevated: 💨 Southwest wind is pushing Sumatra peat smoke across the Straits. Dry laundry indoors & keep N95 masks ready.
hotspots.practicalTipModerate: ⚠️ Moderate fire activity detected in the region. Monitor wind shifts if you have respiratory sensitivity.
hotspots.practicalTipLow: ✅ Low regional fire activity and favorable air dispersion. Safe for regular outdoor routines.
hotspots.guideSubtitle: How satellite fire detections forecast upcoming haze for Malaysia
hotspots.whatIsAsmcDesc: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) uses NOAA and NASA weather satellites with thermal infrared cameras to detect active forest and peatland fires ('hotspots') across Southeast Asia.
hotspots.scaleHigh: 500+: Severe regional crisis (Dense smoke & widespread school alerts)
hotspots.whyWindMattersDesc: Fires alone do not cause haze unless the wind pushes the smoke towards us. During the Southwest Monsoon (June–October), prevailing winds act like an atmospheric conveyor belt, blowing thick peat smoke from Sumatra directly into the Klang Valley, Penang, and the West Coast.
hotspots.decisionsTitle: What This Means For Your Day
hotspots.decisionLaundryDesc: Dry clothes indoors when Sumatra fires are high and winds blow Southwest; otherwise clothes absorb strong smoky odors.
hotspots.decisionSportsDesc: A rising trajectory + Southwest wind means outdoor cardio will stress lungs. Move runs and football games indoors.
hotspots.decisionMasksDesc: Gives you a 24-hour head start to purchase N95/KF94 masks and replace air purifier filters before pharmacy shelves empty.
hotspots.decisionSchoolsDesc: Helps parents anticipate whether schools will cancel outdoor recess or if the MOE API > 200 closure rule might trigger soon.
